intended_object: The standard K-algebra isomorphism K[X_ij : i,j ∈ ι]/(X_ij for j<i, X_ii − 1) ≅ K[X_ij : i<j]. In words, the unlocalized coordinate ring of the upper unitriangular group U_n is a polynomial ring in the strictly upper entries (Milne, item 2.9). I took this from the docstring and the names.
explanation:
How the pieces are built:
- `PolynomialCoordinateRing K ι` is the polynomial ring on the matrix entries (ι×ι) modulo `polynomialIdeal`. That ideal is spanned by `polynomialRelation i j`, which is X_ij when j<i, X_ii − 1 on the diagonal and 0 otherwise. So the quotient is exactly the presentation of U_n before localizing the determinant.
- `FreeCoordinateRing K ι` is `MvPolynomial {p : ι×ι // p.1 < p.2} K`, the free polynomial algebra on the strictly upper entries.
- The equivalence is put together with `AlgEquiv.ofAlgHom` from two maps and the proofs that they are mutually inverse:
  - the lift through the quotient of the map sending each variable to its generic unitriangular entry;
  - `aeval` of the class of X_p.

Mathematically this is correct, and the docstring makes no stronger claim: it explicitly says nothing about Hopf structures.

On generality: K is an arbitrary commutative ring and ι is an arbitrary finite linear order, which is the natural setting for U_n. Mathlib has no unitriangular coordinate ring, so there is no counterpart to cite.
